report.headline: Efficient, high-usage EuroLeague scorer projected for a below-league-average NBA role, with the efficiency read unusable

projection.text: Usage rate is projected to fall to 19.4% in the NBA, down from 25.7% in the EuroLeague and just under the league-average 20.1%; the 80% interval runs from 13.8% to 25.1%, a span of about two league standard deviations, so the model can rank this player but not pin a specific value.

risks.text: The projected 19.4% NBA usage is well below the 26.2% the z-preservation baseline implies if the subject's relative standing carried over fully; the fitted EL->NBA usage slope of 0.579 confirms only about 58% of standing typically transfers on this move.

The true shooting projection offers no real edge over guessing: its 4.7% error ties the naive league-mean baseline, so any apparent efficiency advantage relative to the NBA average of 58.1% should not be relied upon.
The estimate rests on only 61 historical EL->NBA transitions, and the subject's own source-season sample was modest at 874 minutes over 38 games at age 27.0.

Players who make this move already sit +0.46 standard deviations above their own league on average, meaning this projection is conditional on being selected to move, not a generic EuroLeague-to-NBA translation.

strengths.text: In the source season the subject scored 20.638 points per 75 possessions on a 67.1% true shooting percentage, 1.29 standard deviations above the EuroLeague average.

Usage rate of 25.7% stood 1.09 standard deviations above the EuroLeague mean, paired with a 21.1% assist rate and 4.202 assists per 75 possessions, indicating a ball-dominant role with playmaking involvement.
A 15.2% turnover rate at that usage level suggests the high-volume role was not accompanied by excessive giveaways.

uncertainty.text: The true shooting projection of 59.0% should not be treated as informative: the model's out-of-fold error on true shooting (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the league-mean baseline (also 4.7%), so this number is a fallback rather than a genuine estimate.
